hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: A ring that reports an ongoing process where a bar will not fit, beside an icon or inside a dense row. Five sizes cover inline through to prominent, and Upload turns it into a file-transfer control with a cancel action. Unlike Progress Bar it has no property for the amount of progress, so the arc is fixed here and the real value has to come from the implementation.

rows.Description: The smallest ring, for sitting inside a line of text or beside a small icon. The stroke does not thin at this size, so the ring reads as heavy relative to its diameter.
A step up while still inline. The largest size at which the Upload control is not built.
The smallest size that supports Upload, though the control nearly fills the ring at this diameter.
The general-purpose size, and the one where the Upload control sits comfortably inside the ring.
For when progress is the main thing on the surface rather than an inline detail.
Rounds the ends of the progress arc. Despite the name it is a line cap rather than a corner radius, and it only shows where the arc starts and stops.
Squares the arc ends off, for use alongside sharp-shaped controls. The difference is visible at two points on the ring and nowhere else.
A plain progress ring.
Places a file-transfer control at the centre of the ring, reporting the percentage and offering a cancel action. It has no effect at xsmall or xxsmall, where the control is not built.
Shows the unfilled remainder of the ring, which is what makes the arc's extent readable.
Hides it, leaving the arc floating with nothing to measure it against.

rows.What changes: The ring has no hover, pressed, focus or disabled states, and no progress states either. Every one of the ten variants draws the same arc.
A control appears centred in the ring, reporting the percentage. Its own Stop property swaps that readout for a cancel button.

rows.Description: Figma stores no timing and the ring models no transition. The arc is drawn in one fixed position in every variant, so both a determinate sweep and an indeterminate spin belong entirely to the implementation.
There is no property for the amount. The arc sits at roughly three quarters in every variant, which is a placeholder rather than a value, so nothing here should be read as a real state.
Showing or hiding the control does not resize the ring, because the control is centred inside it rather than stacked with it.

The file-transfer control at the centre, left exposed so its Stop state is reachable from the ring. It is a fixed 36px whatever the ring's size, so at small it nearly fills the ring, and at xsmall and xxsmall it is not present at all.
Part of the nested control rather than a property of the ring. It ships reading 75% and has to be overridden on the instance to say anything else.
Neither is a slot. The arc's sweep is what would encode a value, and it is identical in every variant.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: The outer square frame, fixed at the chosen Size, holding the track and the arc concentrically.
Two rings drawn as strokes. The track covers the full circle and the arc covers the portion reported as complete.
A nested control centred in the ring, hidden until Upload is turned on and absent altogether at the two smallest sizes.

sections.title: How to use
dos: Use medium or large whenever Upload is on. The control is a fixed size, so the smaller rings leave it almost no margin.
Pair the ring with nearby text. On its own it says that something is happening but never what.
donts: Don't read the arc as a value. It is identical in every variant, so a screen with several rings will show them all at the same apparent progress.
Don't reach for Upload at xsmall or xxsmall. The property is offered at those sizes but the control is not built, so turning it on does nothing.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: The ring reports progress visually and nothing else. The value, its range and what it refers to all have to be exposed in code.
The ring carries no label of its own, so on its own it signals that something is happening but not what. Pair it with nearby text.
The stroke is the same weight at every size, so at xxsmall the ring is proportionally far heavier than at large. Check the smallest sizes still read as a ring.
The arc and the track are separated by colour alone. Check border/info against border/subtle on the surface behind them.
The Upload control's cancel action is a real control. It needs an accessible name and a keyboard path, neither of which is modelled here.

rows.Description: 24, 36, 40, 48 and 64px across the five steps. Always square, and never hugging its content.
4px (stroke/heavy) at every size. It does not scale, so the ring is roughly a sixth of the diameter at xxsmall and a sixteenth at large.
The track covers the full circle. The arc begins at twelve o'clock and runs about three quarters of the way round, identically in all ten variants.
The arc's ends are round when Rounded is true and square when it is false. The track's ends are always square, though a full circle hides them.
36px regardless of the ring's size, centred, and present only at small, medium and large.

The arc is border/info and the track border/subtle. The arc also carries a foreground/link fill which does not render, because the shape is drawn with no inner area and the stroke does the visible work.
